title: Quarterly Privileged Access Recertification - Notes and Runbook
path: shared_drives/security-and-compliance/Quarterly Privileged Access Recertification - Notes and Runbook.docx
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures planning notes, sampling methodology, automation steps, and the runbook used for the quarterly privileged access recertification (Least-Privilege Recert Q). Primary goals: ensure access entitlements conform to RBAC v2 role model, collect verifiable evidence, ingest relevant events into SIEM, and close exceptions within SLA.

Scope:
- All permanent and temporary privileged roles across Hosted infra (GCP projects), Dedicated admin consoles, Private deployment control plane, and internal tooling (console, admin API).
- Roles in RBAC v2, service-account grants, and membership of privileged groups in identity provider (Okta).
- Exclude ephemeral short-lived tokens already covered by session logging (but verify issuance audit).

Key definitions:
- Privileged entitlement: role or group that grants modify/delete or access to production customer data, cryptographic keys, billing, or deployment pipelines.
- Recertification owner: team listed as owner of the role in RBAC v2 metadata.
- Evidence artifact: timestamped export(s) proving the entitlement exists and the owner attestation (Okta group membership snapshot, IAM policy export, role binding CSV, SIEM event link).

Quarterly schedule (target cycle weeks):
- Week 0: Generate authoritative entitlement exports (RBAC v2 role catalog + IAM bindings + Okta group membership), kick off automated attestation emails to role owners.
- Week 1: Owners review and either approve/adjust via the attestation portal; remediation tickets auto-created for revokes/changes.
- Week 2: Engineering/SRE/Platform triage remediation, complete changes, attach evidence to ticket.
- Week 3: Security QA spot check of remediations and finalize recertification artifact bundle for audit.

Sampling & coverage approach:
Because full-population recertification across all entitlements is costly, we use a hybrid strategy:
- Full recertification for all entitlements flagged as high-risk (customer-data access, KMS/HSM, billing, control plane).
- Stratified random sample (95% CI, 5% margin) for mid-risk roles across teams with >10 members.
- Deterministic check (every quarter) for service accounts, automation principals, and any role modified in last 90 days.
- Any role with no assigned owner escalates to Security for mandatory full review.

Sampling math reference (applied):
- Population N = number of distinct privileged role instances. For mid-risk strata (e.g., N_mid = 420), sample_n = 1.96^2 * p*(1-p)/E^2 adjusted for finite population. Assumed p=0.5 worst-case.

RBAC v2 exports & required fields (authoritative CSV schema):
- fields: ["role_id","role_name","description","privilege_level","owner","owner_email","created_at","last_modified","source_system","attached_permissions_count","attached_groups_count","is_temporary","expiry_if_temporary"]
- Export tip: include the role canonical id (UUID) so we can correlate with audit-log role_id.

Audit log schema mapping (for attestation & SIEM correlation):
- Required event fields: ["timestamp","actor_principal","actor_type","action","resource_type","resource_id","role_id_applied","request_id","ip","user_agent","outcome","raw_payload_link"]
- For RBAC v2 role assignment events we must locate: grant/revoke/role-update with request_id for traceability.

SIEM export & ingestion checklist:
- Ensure the following feeds are present and parsed into the 'privileged_access' sourcetype: Okta system logs (group membership changes), GCP audit logs (policyBinding changes), internal control-plane audit events, and admin-API access logs.
- Parser fields must map to the audit log schema fields above. Use log enrichment to attach 'team_owner' and 'role_risk' tags.
- Retention: privilege-change events retained for minimum 2 years. Evidence snapshots (zip bundles) stored in secure evidence bucket with object immutability for 90 days after quarterly close.

Evidence automation steps (what the automation produces):
1) Run 'rbac-export' job: generate role CSV + role->principal mapping.
2) Run 'idp-snapshot' job: Okta group membership CSV (as-of timestamp).
3) Run 'iam-policy-diff' job: collect recent changes to policies in last 90 days.
4) Correlate exports: join on principal id and role_id to produce a per-entitlement evidence row (CSV + direct SIEM links).
5) Push attestation tasks to portal with prefilled evidence link.

Automation failure modes & mitigations:
- Missing data from cloud provider API: escalate to infra-runner team and mark affected roles as manual-review.
- Duplicate principal identities across identity sources: run identity resolution map; if unresolved, mark as an open exception requiring manual proof.
- SIEM export latency: if the event for a recent grant is not in SIEM within 24 hours, require a direct API snapshot as evidence.

Remediation workflow & SLAs:
- Security ticket auto-created for every denied attestation or owner-requested revoke.
- Triage SLA: security acknowledges ticket within 1 business day.
- Remediation SLA: team must complete change + evidence within 7 business days for high-risk; 14 days for mid-risk; 30 days for low-risk.
- If SLA missed, auto-escalate to the appropriate engineering manager and notify Compliance.

Evidence bundle contents (what to attach to JIRA/Confluence):
- role-catalog.csv (RBAC v2 export), idp-snapshot.csv (Okta), iam-policy.json (raw policy blob), SIEM-event-links.txt (per change), attestation_response.json (portal audit), remediation_ticket_number.
- Hash each bundle file and include SHA256 in ticket comments for integrity.

Manual QA & spot checks (security team):
- For each completed remediation, Security will randomly pick 10% of tickets and re-run the evidence correlation pipeline to ensure outputs match.
- For high-impact roles (KMS, billing), Security does 100% verification.

Exception handling & temporary access path:
- Temporary privileged access must have documented justification, TOTP session, and an explicit expiry <= 7 days unless approved by Exception Board.
- Exceptions repository: Confluence page + Jira key for each exception; exceptions must be re-reviewed at least monthly.

Metrics to report to Compliance (quarterly):
- total_privileged_roles_scoped, percent_recipient_attested, percent_remediated_within_SLA, avg_time_to_remediate, number_open_exceptions, number_manual_reviews_required, number_automation_failures.
- Target KPIs: >= 98% attestation for high-risk; >= 90% remediation within SLA for high-risk.

Attestation portal UX notes (improvements backlog):
- Show last evidence snapshot time and direct SIEM event link inline.
- Allow owners to request temporary role adjustments inline and auto-create remediation tickets prefilled.
- Provide a one-click 'export evidence bundle' for auditors.

Open questions (need decisions before next run):
- Decision: sample size thresholds for teams with frequent churn (Marco to propose per-team multipliers) — due 2026-03-20.
- Decision: whether to shift KMS access to mandatory 30-day forced rotation for service keys — pending product security analysis (Priya).
- Action: Derek to validate that 'role_id' is propagated to the control-plane audit log by 2026-02-28; if not, add compat shim.

Action items (owners & rough dates):
- Aisha: finalize sampling script and publish to security-scripts repo (PR #67) — due 2026-02-19.
- Marco: produce per-team churn multiplier proposal — due 2026-03-20.
- Lena: update SIEM parsers to tag 'role_risk' by 2026-03-05.
- Derek: ensure role_id present in audit events or provide shim — finished 2026-02-27.
- Priya: draft exception-board SOP and approval template — due 2026-03-15.

Audit-readiness checklist (pre-audit):
- All high-risk role bundles present and immutable in evidence bucket.
- All remediation tickets closed or have a documented exception with approval key.
- SIEM queries (saved searches) for time-bounded role changes archived with permalinks.
- Hashes for all evidence files recorded in quarterly audit manifest.

Notes from last run (Q4 2025 retrospective):
- Automation failure rate: 7% (Okta throttling during snapshot window) — mitigation: staggered snapshot and retry with backoff.
- Two mid-risk roles lacked owners; both escalated and assigned during triage.
- Sample size for mid-risk understaffed; increased sample_n by 20% for Q1 2026.

Appendix: quick shell commands / helpers
- rbac-export: ./scripts/rbac-export --as-of YYYY-MM-DD --out /tmp/role-catalog.csv
- idp-snapshot: ./scripts/idp-snapshot --provider okta --out /tmp/okta-snapshot.csv
- evidence-bundle: ./tools/evidence-bundle --ticket SEC-12345 --out ./bundles/SEC-12345.zip
